issues.description: The manuscript gives mutually incompatible accounts of when the interventions occur: after collaborative recall, before collaborative recall, and in the procedure after collaborative recall. This is not a minor procedural detail; the theoretical rationale differs substantially for pre-exposure inoculation versus post-exposure warning/debriefing, and the interpretation of any intervention effect depends on the timing.
issues.quote: "In the present study we decided to place the warning after the collaborative recall" ... "we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation)" ... "The procedure will consist of four main phases: (1) presenting the original material, (2) collaborative recall (including misinformation), (3) three procedures to reduce vulnerability to misinformation"

issues.description: The manuscript states in the procedure that the final individual memory test will use open-ended questions, but the analysis plan later says it will use a two-alternative forced-choice format. These formats measure different constructs, yield different chance levels, require different scoring, and make the power analysis and planned ANOVA ambiguous.
issues.quote: "The test will contain 20 open-ended questions" ... "In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format."

issues.description: The design claims discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced, but the procedure says every pair will discuss the same four critical details. If the same items are always discussed, item difficulty is completely confounded with discussion/misinformation status, preventing a valid within-subject estimate of memory conformity.
issues.quote: "discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced" ... "each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase"

issues.description: Because all pairs discuss the same critical details, any observed difference between discussed and non-discussed details may reflect intrinsic item difficulty, salience, memorability, or response alternatives rather than misinformation exposure. This directly compromises the primary manipulation intended to demonstrate memory conformity.
issues.quote: "In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase. For example, all pairs will talk about Eric’s cap color and his company logo."

issues.description: The proposed ANOVA appears to treat 240 participants as independent observations, but participants are nested within interacting dyads, and randomization is at the pair level. Responses of partners are likely correlated because they see complementary versions, discuss the same items, influence each other, and share the same intervention. Ignoring dyadic clustering will underestimate standard errors and inflate Type I error for intervention effects.
issues.quote: "The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs)." ... "Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups" ... "The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA"

issues.description: The power analysis is based on the number of individual participants rather than the effective number of independent dyads/clusters. Because assignment and interaction occur at the pair level, the between-condition comparison has substantially fewer independent units than assumed, especially if within-pair correlations are nontrivial.
issues.quote: "The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs)." ... "the required sample sizes for the small, medium, and large effects were 664, 112, and 48 participants"

issues.description: The sample size justification for replicating the memory conformity effect averages only two prior effect sizes that differ drastically. A random-effects synthesis with k=2 provides an extremely unstable estimate of the population effect and heterogeneity, making the resulting power calculation unreliable.
issues.quote: "The existing results as regards effect sizes are Hedges’ g = 1.92, N = 55 (Ito et al., 2019) and Hedges’ g = 0.38, N = 74 (Kękuś et al., 2020). Given the rather large difference in effect sizes between both studies, random effects were assumed while calculating the joint effect size"

issues.description: The manuscript converts a pooled Hedges' g from prior studies into Cohen's f for a repeated-measures ANOVA without clearly specifying the standardizer, whether the effect is paired or independent, or how the reported repeated-measures correlation enters the conversion. For a two-level within-subject design, different standardized mean difference definitions produce different f values and different power estimates.
issues.quote: "the joint effect size, which was 1.13. This amounts to a Cohen f of about 0.57. The joint correlation of results in the discussed and non-discussed items in both studies available was 0.07."

issues.subcategory: power based on prior measurement format inconsistent with planned measure
issues.description: The power analysis relies on prior MORI studies using a two-alternative forced-choice test, while the procedure says the present study will use open-ended questions. Open-ended tests typically differ in difficulty, guessing rate, variance, and effect size, so prior forced-choice effect sizes may not support the planned sample size.
issues.quote: "In existing research using the MORI technique a two-alternative forced-choice questions test was used as the main index of correctness of answers." ... "The test will contain 20 open-ended questions"

issues.subcategory: bounded count outcomes analyzed with ANOVA
issues.description: The main dependent variables are counts from a very small number of critical items, likely 0–4 per condition for discussed versus non-discussed critical details. Such bounded, discrete, non-normal data are poorly matched to a standard ANOVA, especially with item and dyad dependence. Item-level binomial or multinomial mixed models would be more appropriate.
issues.quote: "eight of which will cover all the critical details" ... "Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers ... (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers ..." ... "The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA"

issues.subcategory: separate analyses of non-independent response categories
issues.description: Correct answers, misinformation-consistent answers, other answers, and number of answers are not independent outcomes; they are mutually constrained components of the same response process. Running separate ANOVAs on these indices inflates the familywise error rate and can yield incoherent interpretations.
issues.quote: "We will explore the individual memory test’s scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices: the number of correct answers, number of answers consistent with misinformation, other answers, and the overall number of answers."

issues.description: The analysis plan lists multiple dependent variables and additional accuracy summaries without designating a primary endpoint. This creates substantial researcher degrees of freedom in deciding which outcome supports the hypotheses, particularly because accuracy, misinformation endorsement, omissions, and total responding may tell different stories.
issues.quote: "using all four indices: the number of correct answers, number of answers consistent with misinformation, other answers, and the overall number of answers. Moreover, we will observe the individual memory test’s average accuracy on the filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions."

issues.description: The manuscript plans pairwise follow-up comparisons among groups and directional tests but does not specify the exact contrasts, alpha correction, or multiplicity strategy. With four groups, multiple outcomes, and multiple possible pairwise comparisons, Type I error inflation is likely.
issues.quote: "In the case of a significant main interaction, follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed." ... "Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed."

issues.subcategory: conditional follow-up tests conflict with directional hypotheses
issues.description: The authors state ordered predictions about which intervention should be most effective, but the inferential plan relies on an omnibus interaction followed by unspecified pairwise comparisons only if the omnibus test is significant. This does not directly test the predicted ordering and leaves flexibility in interpreting partial patterns.
issues.quote: "we tentatively assume that the most effective technique ... will be Demonstration and motivation" ... "the Extended warning ... is expected to be slightly less effective than Demonstration and motivation but more effective than Education about memory" ... "In the case of a significant main interaction, follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed."

issues.subcategory: accuracy difference is not specific to conformity
issues.description: The primary operationalization of memory conformity as lower accuracy for discussed than non-discussed items is not specific to adopting co-witness misinformation. It can also reflect item difficulty, retrieval practice, output interference, increased uncertainty, response withholding, or exposure to multiple-choice alternatives. Misinformation-consistent responses should be distinguished from mere inaccuracy.
issues.quote: "The correctness of answers to questions concerning discussed and non-discussed details will be compared." ... "The efficacy of a given method will be confirmed if the magnitude of memory conformity (expressed as the difference between the accuracy on discussed and non-discussed items) is smaller"

issues.description: The collaborative task presents each question with five possible responses. This means participants may receive misinformation from the experimental response options, not solely from a co-witness. The construct is therefore not cleanly social memory conformity, because the source of contamination is partly the test format itself.
issues.quote: "Each question and its five possible responses will be displayed in a PowerPoint presentation for 60 seconds while participants discuss the answer."

issues.description: The manuscript repeatedly frames the social phase as collaborative recall, but the actual task is a recognition task with response options. Recall and recognition place different demands on memory and source monitoring, and recognition alternatives can introduce misinformation directly.
issues.quote: "collaborative recall" ... "the participants will complete the collaborative recognition test"

issues.description: The procedure assumes discussed critical items contain misinformation, but partners may not verbalize their discrepant detail, may guess the participant's version, may answer "don't know," or may fail to reach agreement. Without coding actual exposure, the manipulation is heterogeneous and may misclassify non-exposed trials as misinformation trials.
issues.quote: "If the participants are unable to reach an agreement, both responses will be documented." ... "we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner’s differing version of events."

issues.description: The analysis plan first states that a partner response is misleading only if it is actually inconsistent with the participant's version, but then states that all discussed items will be categorized as containing misinformation. These scoring rules can produce different datasets and conclusions.
issues.quote: "if the partner provided an answer consistent with what the participant had seen ... the situation will not be classified as misleading. Of course, the answer ‘don’t know’ will also not be classified as misleading." ... "we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation"

issues.subcategory: no coding protocol or reliability for open-ended responses
issues.description: Open-ended final responses and audio-recorded discussions require coding decisions about spelling, synonyms, partial answers, ambiguous responses, misinformation consistency, and source of partner utterances. The manuscript does not specify coder blinding, number of coders, adjudication procedures, or interrater reliability.
issues.quote: "The discussion will be audio recorded." ... "Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers ... (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers"

issues.description: The experimenter appears to deliver condition-specific interventions and feedback, and no blinding is reported. Knowledge of condition could influence instructions, encouragement, handling of ambiguous discussion, or participant expectations. If the same personnel code outcomes, bias risk is even higher.
issues.quote: "At this moment in this group, the experimenter will give the following information to the participants" ... "In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes."

issues.description: The control podcast is not clearly matched to the active interventions for content relevance, demand characteristics, emotional salience, memory focus, motivation, or expectancy. A podcast on social attitudes may itself influence conformity-related behavior, making it an active and potentially confounding control.
issues.quote: "In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes."

issues.subcategory: interventions not matched for duration and cognitive load
issues.description: The Education and Extended Warning interventions are approximately 7-minute podcasts, whereas Demonstration and motivation includes a DRM task, written recall, feedback, and a motivational podcast. Differences in delay, fatigue, rehearsal opportunity, arousal, and cognitive interference may confound intervention effects.
issues.quote: "The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast" ... "The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast" ... "First ... a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used" ... "Next, the participants’ motivation ... will consist in them listening to a podcast"

issues.description: Because the interventions differ in length and task demands, the delay between viewing/discussion and the final memory test may vary by condition. Any differences in final accuracy could reflect retention interval, fatigue, or interference rather than resistance to misinformation.
issues.quote: "Immediately after the participants are done with the methods of reducing memory conformity (or the control condition), they will complete the individual memory test"

issues.subcategory: DRM task does not demonstrate social influence
issues.description: The Demonstration component uses associative false recall in the DRM paradigm to demonstrate memory fallibility, but memory conformity involves socially supplied post-event misinformation. DRM false memories are not equivalent to vulnerability to co-witness influence, so the manipulation may not instantiate the intended construct.
issues.quote: "in order to demonstrate to participants that they are vulnerable to influence, a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used"

issues.subcategory: DRM manipulation fails for participants without false recall
issues.description: The demonstration depends on participants falsely recalling critical lures. The protocol does not specify what happens when a participant does not write down any lure; for those participants, the intended demonstration of personal vulnerability may fail, creating unequal treatment within the condition.
issues.quote: "The DRM procedure usually results in most of the participants falsely recalling at least a few of the critical lures." ... "See if you have written down any of the words: doctor, window, sweet, thief. If so, you were fooled."

issues.description: The DRM feedback includes the lure "thief" shortly before the final test of a movie in which Eric steals objects. This crime-related prime could alter memory, response criterion, or interpretation of the event independently of the intended intervention.
issues.quote: "See if you have written down any of the words: doctor, window, sweet, thief." ... "The recording shows an electrician (“Eric”) who repairs numerous household devices and also steals a few objects."

issues.description: The three interventions are intended to represent distinct mechanisms, but the authors acknowledge overlap. Extended warning includes education about memory; Demonstration and motivation includes warning, memory fallibility, and motivation. Therefore, differences or similarities across groups cannot be cleanly attributed to the named constructs.
issues.quote: "we are aware of some overlap between the three interventions, for instance, teaching about memory is included is present in a way in both Education about memory and Demonstration and motivation."

issues.description: The theoretical claims attribute expected effects to consistency assumptions, source monitoring, vigilance, motivation, and confidence, but the study does not measure these proposed mediators. Even if an intervention changes memory reports, the planned design cannot identify the mechanism responsible.
issues.quote: "we assumed that the extended warning would cause participants to abandon the consistency assumption, make them more alert to discrepancies" ... "The motivational element of the procedure should furthermore increase the tendency to rely on one’s own recollections."

issues.description: The Extended Warning explicitly tells participants that their partner saw a different version and explains the deception before the final memory test. This may lead participants to strategically avoid partner-consistent answers because they infer the hypothesis, rather than because memory conformity has been reduced.
issues.quote: "Extended warning, informing that the partner actually saw a different version of the movie and informing why the deception was applied" ... "an enlightenment regarding the purpose of the deception"

issues.description: Participants are asked what they think the purpose was only after the final test, and the manuscript describes this only as exploratory. There is no pre-specified plan for excluding, stratifying, or adjusting for participants who detect the deception before or during the final test, even though such awareness directly affects responses.
issues.quote: "Next, the subjects will be requested to say what they think the real purpose of the study was. Their responses will be recorded for exploratory analysis of any relationship between hypothesis awareness and performance."

issues.description: The claim that normative impact is completely ruled out because the final test is individual is too strong. Normative influence can persist after discussion through internalized agreement, concern about later comparison, perceived experimenter expectations, relationship dynamics, or reluctance to contradict a partner. The design does not measure or eliminate these processes.
issues.quote: "we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is no cost of disagreeing."

issues.description: The manuscript does not specify the randomization method, allocation concealment, blocking/stratification, assignment of movie version/glasses/seating, or whether randomization occurs before participant arrival. These details are needed to evaluate selection bias and reproducibility.
issues.quote: "Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups"

issues.subcategory: relationship and familiarity between dyad members uncontrolled
issues.description: Memory conformity is known to vary with familiarity, trust, intimacy, and perceived credibility, yet the recruitment and pairing procedure does not specify whether participants know each other or how familiarity will be measured or controlled. Friends, couples, and strangers may respond very differently.
issues.quote: "The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet." ... "The age of the participants will be restricted"

issues.description: The rationale for the age restriction is to avoid very young participants interacting with elderly participants, but many other dyadic confounds remain, including gender composition, age difference within the 16–35 range, dominance, social status, and relationship type. These factors may affect conformity and intervention efficacy.
issues.quote: "The age of the participants will be restricted in order to avoid a situation in which a very young participant would discuss the original material with an elderly one, which would possibly activate some confounding factors"

issues.description: The MORI procedure depends on visual acuity, polarization, color perception, and ability to hear podcasts/word lists. The manuscript does not specify screening or exclusion criteria for color blindness, visual impairment, hearing impairment, Polish-language proficiency, or inability to wear polarized glasses over corrective lenses.
issues.quote: "Today, you will both be in the 95% visual acuity condition. I will give you each a pair of 95% acuity glasses" ... "The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old"

issues.description: The podcasts are summarized but not provided verbatim. Without scripts, wording, tone, examples, and timing, the interventions cannot be replicated or evaluated for equivalence, demand characteristics, or unintended content differences.
issues.quote: "The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast" ... "The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast" ... "participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes"

issues.description: The DRM word lists, presentation rate, order, instructions, scoring criteria, and prior validation data are not fully reported. The phrase "our previous research" is insufficient for replication and for evaluating whether the manipulation reliably induces false recall in this sample.
issues.quote: "Four lists will be chosen which on the basis of our previous research with this procedure, produce the strongest effect."

issues.description: Although discussions are audio recorded and partner responses determine misinformation exposure, the manuscript does not specify how recordings will be transcribed, coded, temporally segmented, or linked to individual participants, nor whether coders will be blind to condition.
issues.quote: "The discussion will be audio recorded." ... "each answer given by the partner of a participant that is inconsistent with what the participant was presented with is misleading"

issues.description: The final memory test is called individual, but the manuscript does not state whether partners are physically separated, whether they can see each other, or whether the experimenter remains present. Residual social presence could influence reporting and undermine the claim that no interpersonal pressure remains.
issues.quote: "Ultimately, the participants undergo an individual memory test" ... "they will complete the individual memory test of the original material"

issues.description: The only exclusion criterion is "technical problems," which is undefined and leaves discretion after data collection. It is unclear whether exclusions apply to individuals or whole dyads, how peeking, projector misalignment, audio failure, noncompliance, suspicion, or incomplete responses will be handled, and whether excluded participants will be replaced.
issues.quote: "We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session."

issues.description: The manuscript does not describe how missing final-test responses, "don't know" answers, incomplete confidence ratings, unusable audio recordings, participant withdrawal, or exclusion of one member of a dyad will be handled. These omissions affect reproducibility and can bias estimates.
issues.quote: "The test will contain 20 open-ended questions" ... "The discussion will be audio recorded." ... "We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems"

issues.subcategory: no allowance for exclusions in target sample
issues.description: The sample size is fixed at 240, but technical failures and exclusions are anticipated. Without a replacement rule or oversampling plan, the final analyzable sample may fall below the stated power target, especially because one technical failure may compromise both members of a dyad.
issues.quote: "The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs)." ... "We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session."

issues.subcategory: confidence ratings collected without analysis plan
issues.description: The study collects confidence ratings for every answer, and confidence is central to the authors' theoretical account, but no confirmatory analysis plan is provided for these data. This creates flexibility in later reporting and misses an opportunity to test proposed mechanisms.
issues.quote: "for each question, the participants will be asked to rate the subjective certainty of each answer on a scale from 0% ... to 100%"

issues.description: A major theoretical claim is that interventions should work especially for participants aware of discrepancies, yet the design does not include a pre-final-test measure of discrepancy awareness or source monitoring. Post-test guessing of study purpose is not equivalent to item-specific discrepancy awareness.
issues.quote: "we expect that effectiveness of our methods will be higher among people aware of discrepancies between the original information and misinformation than among those unaware of such discrepancies."

issues.subcategory: exploratory DRM predictor measured only in one condition
issues.description: The plan says DRM results will be used as a predictor of MORI performance, but the DRM task is administered only in the Demonstration and motivation group. This limits the analysis to a small, selected subgroup and confounds predictor measurement with intervention exposure.
issues.quote: "As an additional exploratory analysis, the results on the DRM procedure will be used as a possible predictor of the results on the MORI technique." ... "Participants in the DRM group will be given the DRM procedure with feedback"

issues.subcategory: no manipulation checks for intervention comprehension
issues.description: The interventions rely on participants understanding and internalizing warnings, memory education, and motivational content. The manuscript does not include checks of attention, comprehension, perceived credibility, motivation, or memory for intervention content.
issues.quote: "participants will listen to the podcast" ... "The participants will also learn" ... "The participants will be strongly encouraged"

issues.description: The study relies on discussed versus non-discussed items within the same participants. Without a no-discussion control group, it is difficult to separate co-witness contamination from effects of repeated questioning, retrieval practice, response-option exposure, or collaborative retrieval itself.
issues.quote: "The correctness of answers to questions concerning discussed and non-discussed details will be compared."

issues.description: The planned sample is a young convenience sample recruited through media/internet advertisements. Findings may not generalize to older adults, children, actual eyewitnesses under stress, people with lower literacy, or legally relevant witness populations. The manuscript's applied claims should be bounded accordingly.
issues.quote: "The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet."

issues.description: The manuscript frames the study as important for justice systems, but the paradigm uses a silent short film, laboratory dyads, artificial glasses, structured discussion, and immediate testing. These conditions differ from real crimes, stress, delays, police interviews, and natural co-witness conversations.
issues.quote: "research on methods of reducing the memory conformity effect is extremely important for the proper functioning of justice systems" ... "a silent movie that lasts 6 minutes and 34 seconds" ... "One experimental session will last about 60 minutes."

issues.subcategory: ethical procedures for minors and deception omitted
issues.description: The study includes participants as young as 16 and uses deception about visual acuity and different movie versions, but consent/assent, parental consent, ethics approval, risk management, and debriefing details are not specified. These details are necessary for evaluating ethical and procedural feasibility.
issues.quote: "The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old" ... "We are interested in people’s sensory impressions at different levels of visual acuity" ... "Finally, the participants will be debriefed."

issues.description: The manuscript describes the projection setup but does not specify how it will verify that each participant sees only the intended version, that leakage/ghosting is absent, that image brightness is equivalent, or that participants do not notice the dual projection. Such validation is central to MORI data quality.
issues.quote: "Polarizing filters will be placed in front of the lens of each projector: one will be oriented vertically and the other horizontally. Moreover, each participant will receive polarizing glasses that will block one of the two possible versions of the movie."

issues.description: Only examples of critical details are given, and the full set of eight critical details, their alternatives, and their assignment to discussed versus non-discussed status are not reported. Without these details, item difficulty and scoring cannot be evaluated or replicated.
issues.quote: "Both versions are identical except for eight critical details: e.g., in the first version, Eric is trying on a black hat, whereas in the second version the hat is red."

issues.description: The manuscript states that the collaborative test has 12 questions and five possible responses per question but does not provide the questions, alternatives, whether alternatives include both versions, or how response order is randomized. These details are essential because the alternatives themselves may introduce misinformation.
issues.quote: "The test will comprise 12 questions, four of which refer to critical details ... with the other eight being control questions. Each question and its five possible responses will be displayed"

issues.subcategory: intervention effects confounded with response criterion
issues.description: The interventions may reduce misinformation-consistent answers by making participants more conservative or more likely to say "don't know," not by improving memory or resistance to conformity. The planned efficacy criterion based on accuracy difference does not clearly distinguish improved memory accuracy from altered willingness to answer.
issues.quote: "Participants ... will be strongly encouraged to rely only on their own memory" ... "Four indices will be derived ... (4) the overall number of answers." ... "The efficacy of a given method will be confirmed if ... the difference between the accuracy on discussed and non-discussed items is smaller"

issues.subcategory: weak transfer from persuasion inoculation to memory conformity
issues.description: The Demonstration and motivation intervention is justified using persuasion-resistance research about illegitimate authority in advertisements, but the target phenomenon is source monitoring and memory report after co-witness discussion. The theoretical bridge is plausible but underspecified, and the planned design does not test whether persuasion-inoculation mechanisms operate here.
issues.quote: "This was inspired by existing research on resisting social influence presented by Sagarin, Cialdini, Rice, & Serna (2002). Their technique was based on the inoculation theory" ... "We adapted the ideas from the research described above in the hope that it may be useful in mitigating memory conformity."

issues.description: The planned ANOVA aggregates across a very small set of critical items and does not model items as a source of variance. This is especially problematic because critical details can differ greatly in memorability and because item status may not be counterbalanced as claimed.
issues.quote: "eight of which will cover all the critical details" ... "The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA"

issues.subcategory: representativeness claim conflicts with cited samples and planned sampling
issues.description: The power section refers to prior data as coming from a representative Polish sample, but the cited sample sizes are small experimental samples, and the planned sample is a convenience sample recruited through advertisements. The representativeness basis is unclear and potentially misleading.
issues.quote: "the same procedure as that planned in the proposed study was used on a representative Polish sample" ... "The participants ... will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet."
